content: 1. Hotez PJ and colleagues developed a multivalent anthelmintic vaccine aimed at preventing hookworm and schistosomiasis. This work was published in the Expert Review of Vaccines in 2008, volume 7, issue 6, pages 745–752. 2. Lustigman S and Abraham D provided an in-depth discussion on onchocerciasis in the book Vaccines for Biodefense and Emerging and Neglected Diseases, edited by Barrett ADT and Stanberry LR, published by Academic Press Inc Elsevier Science & Technology in 2009. Their contribution is found in chapter 67, pages 1379–1400. 3. Hotez PJ and colleagues explored the development of vaccines targeting hookworm infections, as detailed in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 1997, volume 16, issue 10, pages 935–940. 4. Bergquist R and Lustigman S emphasized the importance of vaccine development as a critical component in controlling significant helminthic infections. Their findings were published in Advances in Parasitology in 2010, volume 73, pages 297–326. 5. Ngoumou P, Walsh JF, and Mace JM introduced a rapid mapping technique to assess the prevalence and distribution of onchocerciasis, using a case study from Cameroon. This was published in the Annals of Tropical Medicine and Parasitology in 1994, volume 88, issue 5, pages 463–474. 6. Lengeler C and colleagues demonstrated the utility of community-based questionnaires and health statistics as cost-effective tools for identifying communities at risk of urinary schistosomiasis. Their work appeared in the International Journal of Epidemiology in 1991, volume 20, issue 3, pages 796–807. 7. Wanjí S and colleagues combined rapid assessment procedures for loiasis (RAPLOA) and onchocerciasis (REA) in rain forest villages of Cameroon. Their findings were published in the Filaria Journal in 2005, volume 4, issue 1, article 2. 8. Boatin BA and Richards FO Jr. reviewed strategies for controlling onchocerciasis in Advances in Parasitology in 2006, volume 61, pages 349–394. 9. Boatin BA and colleagues compared three diagnostic methods for detecting Onchocerca volvulus infection in low-prevalence areas. This study was published in Parasitology in 2002, volume 125, issue 6, pages 545–552. 10. Chambers EW and colleagues evaluated xenomonitoring of Wuchereria bancrofti and Dirofilaria immitis infections in mosquitoes from American Samoa. They compared polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays with dissection methods, as detailed in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2009, volume 80, issue 5, pages 774–781. 11. Lipner EM and colleagues assessed the field applicability of a rapid-format anti-Ov-16 antibody test for monitoring onchocerciasis control measures in endemic regions. Their study was published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2006, volume 194, issue 2, pages 216–221. 12. Lammie PJ and colleagues conducted a multicenter trial to evaluate recombinant antigen-based antibody assays for diagnosing and surveilling lymphatic filariasis. This work appeared in the Filaria Journal in 2004, volume 3, issue 1, article 9. 13. Mladonicky JM and colleagues used parasitologic, serologic, and entomologic tools to assess lymphatic filariasis transmission after mass drug administration in American Samoa. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2009, volume 80, issue 5, pages 769–773. 14. Cringoli G introduced the FLOTAC apparatus, a novel multivalent fecal egg count technique, in Parassitologia in 2006, volume 48, issue 3, pages 381–384. 15. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a report in 2009 on the elimination of schistosomiasis from low-transmission areas, following an informal consultation held in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, on August 18–19, 2008. 16. Zhu YC reviewed the role of immunodiagnosis in schistosomiasis control in China, as published in Acta Tropica in 2005, volume 96, issues 2–3, pages 130–136. 17. Lier T and colleagues developed a real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay for detecting low-intensity Schistosoma japonicum infections in China. Their study was published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2009, volume 81, issue 3, pages 428–432. 18. Handali S and colleagues developed and evaluated a magnetic immunochromatographic test for detecting Taenia solium, the causative agent of taeniasis and neurocysticercosis in humans. This work appeared in Clinical and Vaccine Immunology in 2010, volume 17, issue 4, pages 631–637. 19. The WHO Technical Report Series No. 972 (2012) outlined research priorities for helminth infections, as part of the TDR Disease Reference Group's technical report on helminth infections. 20. Guezala MC and colleagues developed a species-specific coproantigen ELISA for diagnosing human Taenia solium taeniasis. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2009, volume 81, issue 3, pages 433–437. 21. Taylor HR and colleagues evaluated the sensitivity of skin snips for diagnosing onchocerciasis in Tropical Medicine and Parasitology in 1987, volume 38, issue 2, pages 145–147. 22. Stingl P and colleagues introduced a diagnostic patch test for onchocerciasis using topical diethylcarbamazine, as published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 1984, volume 78, issue 2, pages 254–258. 23. Lindblade KA and colleagues documented the elimination of Onchocerca volvulus transmission in the Santa Rosa focus of Guatemala, as detailed in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2007, volume 77, issue 2, pages 334–341. 24. Rodríguez-Pérez MA and colleagues compared the sensitivity of a cocktail of recombinant antigens used in an indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) with a rapid-format antibody card test for detecting Onchocerca volvulus. This study was published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2003, volume 97, issue 5, pages 539–541. 25. Burbelo PD and colleagues developed a four-antigen mixture for the rapid assessment of Onchocerca volvulus infection, as published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2009, volume 3, issue 5, article e438.
